description:
Project Overview

TU Delft is recruiting a doctoral researcher to coordinate AI agents managing radio, transport, computing and service resources in future 6G networks. The position belongs to the Future Network Services programme.

Research Position Overview

Develop online-learning and distributed decision-making methods under incomplete information. Study multi-domain resource allocation, fault diagnosis, root-cause analysis and autonomous remediation, and evaluate proposed methods with programme partners and experimental infrastructure.

Research Areas

  • Agentic AI
  • 6G resource management
  • Online learning

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPhD researcher
Salary€3,204–€4,051 gross per month, depending on doctoral year.
DurationFour years: an initial 18-month contract, followed by 30 months subject to a positive assessment.
Programme / host supportFuture Network Services programme; salaried doctoral employment.
Benefits8% holiday allowance, 8.3% year-end bonus and pension arrangements.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic preparation and appointment conditions
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityWorldwide applicants may be considered subject to academic eligibility, recruitment checks and the stated appointment conditions.
Academic preparationCompleted or nearly completed MSc in computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics or a related field.
Research skillsInterest in constrained learning, distributed optimisation, game theory and reliable network operation.
LanguageEnglish proficiency meeting TU Delft doctoral admission requirements.

Recruitment dates and location

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 1 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  • CV showing universities attended and study durations.
  • Motivation letter of no more than half a page.
  • BSc and MSc degree certificates and complete transcripts.

Submit through the application system linked from the official vacancy. Follow its current document and translation instructions.

Selection and Contact

Apply only once to the best-fitting of the four related Future Network Services vacancies; the team can assess fit with other research lines.

Research contact: Dr Georgios Iosifidis.

About TU Delft

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, Netherlands. This appointment combines supervised research with doctoral training through the university’s Graduate School.
